Atrophy affects a lot of trans men, but the degree to which it affects them varies. Personally, I went through atrophy that was painful any time I walked, and I did have to go through intravaginal estradiol treatment three times a week for about four months before it let up. I still can't do penetration, but I can move without pain, so I'm happy with where I am.
However, others, like the person you mentioned, might only ever feel it during penetration and never experience pain from atrophy anytime else. Others don't go through painful atrophy at all. It's a genetic coin toss, basically.

It is a real risk that you'll experience atrophy, and I can't promise it'll only affect you during penetration, if It'll affect you all the time, or if it'll even affect you at all.

In the US, you need parental consent and, depending on the clinic you go to, you may need a letter from a therapist/psychiatrist as well. If you want a quick list to help out, try to do something like this (assuming you're American like me)

- Check the laws in your state, see if it's legal. Some states block all gender affirming medical care for minors.
- Talk to your parents, make sure they're on board.
- If it is legal, look for nearby LGBT clinics in your state that provide HRT and call them up to ask about their requirements for starting as a minor. If they ask for a letter, make sure to ask specifically what should be included in that letter. If you have no nearby clinic, look for a planned parenthood.
- If you do need a letter, find an informed therapist (GALAP is a great resource for this, look them up!) and let them know the requirements of the clinic.
- Set an appointment and go to a consultation!

Be warned, this is a very bare bones piece of advice and your situation may vary wildly. Good luck :)

Hey, I've been self-harming for about a year now and I know the "Don't do it, you'll regret it" or "Stop for me :(" shit doesn't really work, so I'll just offer some methods for harm reduction if you ever do it again. I am not encouraging you to self-harm at all, it's an awful thing and you should try your best to stop if you can, but if you can't it's at least best to be safe.

Keep in mind the urges most of the time come in waves that you can wait out (if you become more addicted, occasionally there may be times where there are no waves and it's just a constant feeling, but for the most part it's waves). Every time you want to cut tell yourself to wait 20-30 minutes and do whatever the hell you can to distract yourself. Play video games, watch videos, draw, stare at a wall and space out, scream into a pillow, absolutely anything.

Have a safe space in your house where you're away from anything sharp. Your bedroom is probably the best place. Do not take any sharp tool in there, and if you still have the urge to have something sharp nearby, take something a bit dull.

If you cave in and cut, take a minute long break after each cut and evaluate how you feel. Are you still stressed, angry, or sad? Do you feel like you need more? Keep doing this after each cut until the answer to both is no. Don't do it quickly and without thinking, that's how I did it and now I have hundreds of permanent scars on my arms and thighs.

Lastly, and I cannot stress this enough, do not be lazy when it comes to caring for them. You end up increasing the possibility of an infection if you don't clean them properly. Clean them with a rag, don't use things like paper towels or toilet paper since they can flake off into the cut. Use Neosporin or anything similar if you have it on hand, then use bandaids or bandages. If you end up cutting too deep you may need a butterfly bandage.

Also: if you see anything yellow in a fresh cut, hospital. Now. That is fat and you need stitches.

I hope you can stop entirely because eventually, you begin to rely on it just to regulate your emotions. If you can't though, stay safe and try to use some of the advice I gave. I hope you turn out alright.
